suggestions: Specify exact post-MI complication being tested (VSD, free wall rupture, papillary muscle rupture with MR, LV aneurysm, pericarditis/Dressler syndrome, RV infarction, mural thrombus)
Provide actual ECG findings for interpretation (e.g., new conduction defects for septal rupture, persistent ST elevation for aneurysm, PR depression for pericarditis)
Provide actual echo findings for interpretation (e.g., colour Doppler showing VSD shunt, severe MR jet, apical akinesis with thrombus, pericardial effusion)
Include haemodynamic data consistent with complication (e.g., increased JVP for RV infarction, cardiogenic shock parameters for free wall rupture)
Add specific examination findings (e.g., harsh pansystolic murmur at left sternal edge for VSD, apical pansystolic murmur radiating to axilla for MR, pericardial rub for pericarditis)
Provide management guidance specific to complication (e.g., urgent cardiothoracic surgery for VSD, anticoagulation contraindication for free wall rupture risk, NSAIDs for Dressler syndrome)
Use RANZCR systematic reporting structure for echo (LV function, wall motion abnormalities, valvular assessment, pericardium, conclusion with complication named)
Include differential diagnosis in expected answers (mechanical vs electrical vs inflammatory post-MI complications)

agent_evaluations.detailed_feedback: This OSCE station fails to meet Australian radiology interpretation standards due to complete lack of actual diagnostic content. The scenario is a placeholder template with no specific post-MI complication identified, no real imaging findings described, and no systematic interpretation framework provided. For radiology evaluation: (1) Post-MI complications are time-sensitive diagnoses requiring systematic ECG analysis (conduction abnormalities, ST segment evolution, arrhythmias) and focused echo assessment (wall motion, valves, shunt detection, pericardium). (2) The current content cannot be used for teaching or assessment as students have no actual images or findings to interpret. (3) Australian radiological standards require structured reports with specific findings, not generic placeholder text. (4) AMC Clinical Examination radiology stations test systematic interpretation skills using real imaging findings. CRITICAL REMEDIATION REQUIRED: Content generator must select a specific post-MI complication (e.g., 'Day 4 post-anteroseptal STEMI, now with new harsh pansystolic murmur and cardiogenic shock - ECG shows new RBBB, echo shows 1.5cm apical VSD with left-to-right shunt'), provide actual interpretation findings, and create RANZCR-compliant expected answers. Current version is unsuitable for any educational or assessment purpose.
agent_evaluations.educational_value: INADEQUATE - Content is placeholder template only, provides no learning opportunity for radiology interpretation of post-MI complications
clinical_safety_concerns: Generic vital signs mask haemodynamic instability that characterises mechanical post-MI complications (VSD, free wall rupture, acute MR) - risk of students not recognising cardiogenic shock

Absence of specific complication timeline prevents teaching critical time-dependent diagnosis (VSD/free wall rupture at day 3-5 require urgent surgery; Dressler syndrome at weeks 2-10 managed medically)
No mention of urgent cardiothoracic surgery referral for mechanical complications - these are surgical emergencies with high mortality if delayed
agent_evaluations.recommendation: REJECT - Requires complete regeneration with specific post-MI complication selected, actual ECG and echo findings provided, systematic RANZCR interpretation framework applied, and time-appropriate haemodynamic data included. Cannot be used in current form.
